title: Hoodie and Shorts — The Best Fall Combo
note: Every price read off the brand's own store on 18 Sept 2026, from the US storefront where the brand runs one. Walker Golf Things prices in USD at walkergolfthings.com/en-us (their default Australian storefront shows AUD); Sounder prices in GBP. Nothing is converted. No repeat brands within a section.
hoodies: Organic cotton with a brushed terry inside, and a Tiger caricature on the chest that nobody has to explain. The cheapest way into this list and the one most likely to get a comment at the turn.
Plain black, small mark, no argument. RGC built its whole thing on municipal golf being the good kind, and the hoodie reads the same way — it does not care where you are playing.
Spade Polar Fleece Pullover Hoodie · Grey
Polar fleece rather than French terry, which means it traps more air and weighs less. The one on this list to reach for when the dawn number actually starts with a five.

Brushed cotton-poly fleece out of Melbourne, with a felt appliqué logo at the chest and a Kooka patch on the left sleeve. Marked down from $129.95 in their Back Nine sale as of 18 September, which makes it the best value on this list.
Sugarloaf design for the parking lot and the fire pit as much as the first tee, and the Camp Hoody is the clearest version of that. Silver sage is the colour that goes with every short below.
Radry is a drawing studio that happens to sell clothes, and the Staple is the piece where the drawing steps back. Athletic grey, heavyweight, nothing else going on.
Cable-knit texture on a hooded body, which is a strange idea until you see it on. Reads as a sweater from ten feet and a hoodie from two.
Cotton cut with modal and a little nylon, so it drapes rather than boxes. Quiet Golf makes exactly one hoodie and has evidently spent the whole budget on it.
The Fesque is Malbon's permanent-collection hoodie — 100% cotton fleece, double-layer hood, script across the chest. It is the piece the rest of their calendar hangs off.
Screen-printed rather than embroidered, which is the whole Metalwood argument — the graphic should look like it came off a 1970s pro shop wall, not a corporate uniform program.
Actual Polartec, not fleece-adjacent marketing. This is the one on the list built to be played in rather than pulled on afterwards — it breathes when you start swinging.
Knit, cut and sewn in Japan by Minami Co., a textile house that has been running since 1935. Sentinel is known here for bags; this is the piece that argues they are an apparel brand too.
shorts_casual: Cotton corduroy, cut for sitting down in. Brooklyn's muni label has a talent for the piece you forget you are wearing.
The Terry Short x Byrdie · Bottle Green
Terry cloth, from the Byrdie collaboration, and there is a matching anorak if you want to commit. The most couch-forward thing on this page and it knows it.
Wide-wale cotton cord, elastic waist and drawcord, six-inch inseam. Corduroy in September sounds wrong and looks completely right.
Basketball mesh, sold by a golf brand, with no apology anywhere in the product copy. These are the football-watching shorts and everybody already knows it.
A poly-wool slack cut baggy and pleated. Students calls it their most popular short, which tracks — it is the one that passes in a restaurant.
Seersucker puckers away from the skin, which is exactly the trick you want when the afternoon turns. Cut short and loose in a way that suits the fabric.
shorts_golf: Marked down from $69.95 as of 18 September. The entry point on the list, and a perfectly straight technical short with nothing to prove.
Named for the range because that is where the brand started — two founders, a logo of a man mid-swing in jeans, and a point to make about who golf belongs to.
Named for the pockets, which are deep enough to be the point — a tee pocket at the back hip, zip side pockets and an internal ball-marker pocket in a 2-way stretch micro-ripstop.
A drawcord waist on a technical short — the detail that lets one pair cover the round and the rest of the day. Priced in pounds sterling on Sounder's own store.
Manors cut their shorts longer than the American house style, closer to a trouser that stops at the knee. Vintage indigo reads denim from a distance.
Coolcore is a fabric treatment that moves moisture to cool the surface rather than just wicking it away. In a Texas October that is not a gimmick.
